hardware.device: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S Graphics

candidate.description: Capture all 127 position-specialized decode transitions into one multi-stream HIP graph. Device-published token and position state feed each transition into the next, and fixed graph nodes preserve each global-attention live count.

protocol.command: GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2 HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 HIPENGINE_HIP_ARCH=gfx1151 HIPENGINE_COMPILER_VERSION_FILE=/tmp/laguna_hipcc_version.txt HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1 PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python3 -u scripts/laguna_long_context_profile.py --context-length 4096 --lengths 512 --chunk-size 2048 --decode-output-tokens 128 --repetitions 1 --warmup-rows 128 --compiler-version-file /tmp/laguna_hipcc_version.txt --require-cached-build --compare-decode-graph --allow-dirty --output /tmp/laguna-decode-graph-first-screen.json
attempt_notes: Attempt 1 failed before capture because the temporary graph module imported the embedding launcher from the wrong module.
Attempt 2 failed before capture because bulk prefill does not use decode control publication.
Attempt 3 seeded the exact token, scratch-position, and KV-row-position scalars and completed with exact output.

decision.interpretation: A giant whole-window ROCm graph is slower than direct two-queue submission even after excluding capture. Vulkan's command-buffer batching does not transfer profitably as one approximately 61k-node HIP graph on this stack.
decision.next: Prefer small exact fusion/composite boundaries that remove kernels and device work, or separately test bounded per-token graph units only if dynamic global-attention metadata can avoid frozen live-count scalars.
